## The defect

The `organizations.*` key family was renamed from "organization" to "workspace" terminology in **en** and **zh** only. The other eight packs had **exactly one** key — `create` — follow, leaving each pack internally inconsistent. `de.ts` is the clearest specimen:

```
create:            "Workspace erstellen"      ← workspace
mine:              "Meine Organisationen"     ← organization
title:             "Organisationen"
heading:           "Ihre Organisationen"
searchPlaceholder: "Organisation suchen"
new:               "Neue Organisation"
current:           "Aktuelle Organisation"
```

**These keys render next to each other in one dropdown.** Since PR #4638 restored the avatar menu's "My Workspaces" entry, a German user sees `Meine Organisationen` directly above `Workspace erstellen` — two names for one object, two lines apart. It was invisible before that PR because `organizations.mine` had no call site; it is on screen now, in eight languages.

## ⛔ Zone 1 — answer the namespace question BEFORE editing anything

The card is explicit and this is the one way to get it badly wrong:

> Worth checking whether the sibling `organization.*` family (org **management**) was meant to follow the rename at all … **The two families are separated on purpose** (there is a comment between them in `en.ts`).

So: **read that comment in `en.ts` first.** My reading of the evidence — verify it, do not inherit it — is that `en` and `zh` already show the intended end state: the **plural `organizations.*` picker family** became "workspace", and the **singular `organization.*` management family** did not. If the tree bears that out, your radius is the plural family in eight packs and nothing else.

⛔ **A find-and-replace over `organization`/`workspace` would destroy a separation that exists deliberately.** Scope by namespace, never by string. If the tree does *not* settle the question cleanly, **stop and report** rather than guessing — a wrong answer here silently renames a management surface in eight languages.

## Zone 2 — what "done" looks like

Bring the eight packs' `organizations.*` family into line with the terminology `en` and `zh` already use, across all the keys that carry the noun: `mine`, `title`, `heading`, `subtitle`, `searchPlaceholder`, `new`, `current`, plus `emptyTitle` / `emptyDescription` / `noMatches`.

**This is translation, not string substitution.** Each language has its own established term for a workspace (`Arbeitsbereich`, `espace de travail`, `ワークスペース`, `작업 공간`, …) — the existing `create` key in each pack already committed to one, since that is the single key that followed the rename. **Use each pack's own existing choice as the reference** rather than inventing a second term for the same object in the same file. If a pack's `create` key does not settle it, say which and why in the PR.

## Zone 3 — why no gate caught this, and what it implies for tests

The card measured this and it is worth keeping: `all-locales-key-parity` is green because every pack **has** every key; `check:i18n-drift` follows changes to the **en** value and en has not moved; `check:i18n-keys` compares call sites and inline defaults against **en** only, so the eight non-en packs are outside its comparison set. It is a same-language *vocabulary* inconsistency, which nothing in place looks for.

I am **not** asking you to build a vocabulary gate — that is a different card and a hard problem. But do consider whether a cheap pin is available for *this* family specifically (e.g. no `organizations.*` value in any pack still carries the old noun), and if you conclude one is not worth it, say so rather than leaving it unmentioned.

## Gates

Derive from your diff — expect `Lint`, `Type Check`, the test shards, the i18n gate family, `Control Byte Scan` (locale files carry non-ASCII, so scan the changed files directly too). Changeset required (`@object-ui/i18n`, patch).

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #5215`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report **and** post it as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`. Note this card was **moved from `objectstack-ai/objectstack#8669`** today — the original thread there has a comment that was not copied. Check the body for sanitizer truncation before relying on it.

## The namespace question was answered from the tree, not assumed

This was the one way to get the card badly wrong, and it was closed properly: confirmed in `en.ts` that `organizations.*` (plural, picker) and `organization.*` (singular, management) are **deliberately separate**, per the comment between the blocks — **and** found an existing `organization-namespace-3546` test that already pins that separation. So the answer came from two independent artifacts rather than from my reading of the evidence, which is what I asked for.

A find-and-replace over `organization`/`workspace` would have destroyed that separation in eight languages at once. It was scoped by namespace instead.

## Translation, not substitution — verified in the shape of the diff

Ten noun-carrying keys per pack, brought into line with **each pack's own workspace term**, which its unchanged `create` key had already committed to. The report states gender/definiteness/particle agreement was adjusted **per key** rather than a literal string swap — and the diff shape corroborates it: exactly 20 changed lines per file for 10 keys, i.e. every key rewritten individually rather than a uniform token replacement.

That is the difference between "the words now match" and "the sentences are correct in eight languages", and only the second is worth shipping.

## The gate hole got a pin rather than a shrug

The card's sharpest point was that **no existing gate could see this**: `all-locales-key-parity` is green because every pack *has* every key; `check:i18n-drift` follows changes to the **en** value and en had not moved; `check:i18n-keys` compares against **en** only, so the eight packs sit outside its comparison set. A same-language vocabulary inconsistency was invisible to all three.

The new `organizations-picker-vocabulary-5215.test.ts` closes exactly that class, and it is pinned **in both directions** — no `organizations.*` picker value still carries the pack's old organization-noun, **and** `organization.*` still does. The second half is what stops a future over-eager rename from quietly erasing the separation this card just confirmed. I asked the dev to consider whether a cheap pin existed and to say so if not; it found one and it is the right shape.

**Verification:** full `packages/i18n` suite green (47 files, 840 tests) including the new pin, `all-locales-key-parity`, and `organization-namespace-3546`; `check-i18n-en-drift` reports **0 en values changed**, independently confirming en/zh were not touched.
